$comment: The interpolation findings both analyses give the files of the test project in this folder, copied verbatim from the user's interpolationtests project, where every form of A to C also writes query, text from the request, somewhere it does harm, and D_EveryPosition.kt writes every kind of value into every position, with what the editor must say above each line, as E_Interpolate.kt does for calls to interpolate: analyzeKotlin in editors/vscode/src/analyze.ts and Analyzer.analyzeKotlin in streamlord-analysis, each file on its own, with the const vals the workspace declares (constants) known, as the VS Code index and IntelliJ provide them. Only the interpolation codes are listed (kotlin-interpolation, unescaped-interpolation, unsafe-interpolation, interpolate-template, interpolate-placeholders), and missing-id and top-level-text must not appear in any file. Offsets count UTF-16 code units; line is for the reader. What IntelliJ adds with types is in the plugin's own InspectionTest.

E_Interpolate.kt.message: Kotlin fills in $query before interpolate sees the markup, so interpolate neither escapes nor refuses it. Make it a %s placeholder and pass the value to interpolate.
Kotlin fills in ${applicant.name} before interpolate sees the markup, so interpolate neither escapes nor refuses it. Make it a %s placeholder and pass the value to interpolate.

Kotlin fills in ${query} before interpolate sees the markup, so interpolate neither escapes nor refuses it. It lands in data-on:click, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path. Put the value in an attribute of its own, such as data-label, and read it in the expression with el.dataset.label.

Kotlin interpolates $count here, as the whole Datastar expression. Meant as a server value, only a number or a boolean is safe there; meant as the signal $count, make the whole literal $$"""...""" (Kotlin 2.2+), or escape as ${'$'}count.
interpolate throws IllegalArgumentException here: the markup has 2 %s placeholders and 1 value is given. Write %% for a per cent sign that is not a placeholder.
interpolate throws IllegalArgumentException here: the markup has 1 %s placeholder and 2 values are given. Write %% for a per cent sign that is not a placeholder.
interpolate throws IllegalArgumentException here: the markup has 0 %s placeholders and 1 value is given. Write %% for a per cent sign that is not a placeholder.

interpolate always throws here: query lands in data-text, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path, and only a number or a boolean is let in there. Put the value in an attribute of its own, such as data-label, and read it in the expression with el.dataset.label.

interpolate throws here unless applicant.name is a number or a boolean: it lands in data-text, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path. Put the value in an attribute of its own, such as data-label, and read it in the expression with el.dataset.label.
interpolate always throws here: hidden lands in style, which is read as CSS, and only a number is let in there. Pass a number and write the unit in the markup, or choose between classes.

interpolate always throws here: query lands in the markup's own structure, a tag name, an attribute name or an unquoted value, and only Trusted(...) is let in there. Build that part of the markup from literals, or quote the attribute value; wrap markup you built yourself in Trusted(...).

interpolate always throws here: query lands in the markup's own structure, a tag name, an attribute name or an unquoted value, and only Trusted(...) is let in there. Build that part of the markup from literals, or quote the attribute value; wrap markup you built yourself in Trusted(...).

interpolate always throws here: query lands in a script or style element, which the browser runs, and only Trusted(...) is let in there. Put the value in a data-* attribute and read it from there; wrap markup you built yourself in Trusted(...).

interpolate always throws here: interpolate("%s", quer… lands in data-text, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path, and only a number or a boolean is let in there. Put the value in an attribute of its own, such as data-label, and read it in the expression with el.dataset.label.
Kotlin fills in ${applicant.errors.joinToString…} before interpolate sees the markup, so interpolate neither escapes nor refuses it. Make it a %s placeholder and pass the value to interpolate.

Kotlin fills in $inner before interpolate reads the markup, so interpolate reads what it holds as markup too: a %s in it is a placeholder and a %% a per cent sign, and interpolate throws or changes the markup. Make it a %s placeholder and pass the Html: interpolate writes an Html or a Trusted there as it is.
